instructions:
### ROLE ###
You maintain a small, growing set of CONCEPT SCHEMES (entity categories) for a knowledge registry built from cybersecurity incident reports. A group of entities extracted from several reports has just been found to be close to each other and far from every existing scheme. Decide whether the group is a genuinely new scheme or an alias of an existing one, and name it.

### EXISTING SCHEMES ###
- Security Vulnerability: A flaw or weakness in software, hardware, or a system that can be exploited to compromise security.
- Software Product: An application, operating system, or suite of computer programs designed to perform specific tasks or functions.
- Software Vendor: An organization or company that develops, distributes, or maintains software, hardware, or related technology products and services.
- Country: A distinct territorial body or sovereign state with its own government and defined geographical borders.
- Government Organization: An official agency, ministry, or administrative body operating as part of a national or state government.
- Malware: Malicious software, code, or executables designed to infiltrate, damage, or compromise computer systems and data.
- Uniform Resource Locator: A standardized web address specifying the location and retrieval mechanism of a resource on a computer network.
- Person: An individual human being, such as a government official, cybersecurity expert, researcher, or executive.
- IP Address: A numerical label assigned to a device connected to a computer network that uses the Internet Protocol for communication.
- Email Address: A unique identifier used to send and receive electronic mail messages over a computer network.
- Computer File: A digital resource or named item stored on a computer system, containing data, code, or instructions.
- Company: A commercial business, corporation, or enterprise operating in any economic sector or industry.

### THE GROUP ###
Each line is one entity with the description written at extraction time:
- rmssrv4[.]ru [domain name] — An internet domain name used for remote connection server infrastructure.
- rmssrv2[.]ru [domain name] — An internet domain name used for remote connection server infrastructure.
- rmssrv3[.]ru [domain name] — An internet domain name used for remote connection server infrastructure.
- mx-out-14.default-host.net [domain name] — A mail server domain name observed in the HELO header of phishing emails.
- 1833.site [domain name] — A domain name used to distribute malicious executable files.
- gov-ua.info [domain name] — A domain name used in a spoofing campaign mimicking Ukrainian government sites.

### RULES ###
- A scheme is a KIND of entity (e.g. "Hacker group", "Malware family", "Software product", "Government body", "Internet domain", "Country"), never a role in an incident and never a single entity.
- Return `"verdict": "alias-of"` with `"target"` set to an existing scheme's label when the group is the same kind as that scheme (different wording, same meaning). Judge by MEANING of the descriptions, not by surface words.
- Return `"verdict": "new"` when no existing scheme covers the group. Then give:
  - `prefLabel`: a short English noun phrase, 1–3 words, singular, Title Case (e.g. "Malware Family").
  - `definition`: one sentence, at most 25 words, stating what belongs to the scheme, general enough to hold across reports.
  - `altLabels`: 0–3 alternative English labels.
- If the group mixes clearly different kinds, name the kind of the MAJORITY and list the minority entity names in `outliers`.
- If uncertain between alias and new, prefer `new`: an extra scheme can be merged later; a wrong merge cannot be undone cheaply.

### OUTPUT ###
A single raw JSON object, no markdown fences, no commentary:
{ "verdict": "new" | "alias-of", "target": "<existing label or null>", "prefLabel": "...", "definition": "...", "altLabels": [...], "outliers": [...] }
text: Decide and name the group now.
response: {"verdict": "new", "target": null, "prefLabel": "Domain Name", "definition": "A human-readable identification string defining a realm of administrative autonomy or resource location within the Internet Domain Name System.", "altLabels": ["Internet Domain", "FQDN", "Fully Qualified Domain Name"], "outliers": []}
